task_3.title: Accept JWKs without a use claim as signing keys
task_3.description: The JWKS client now treats keys with no declared JWK use as eligible signing keys instead of rejecting them outright. This aligns signing-key discovery with RFC7517 semantics for an omitted use claim while preserving the existing requirement that usable signing keys expose a key ID and that an error is raised when no eligible signing keys are available.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that JWKS signing-key discovery accepts JWK entries whose `use` claim is omitted, so valid signing keys are not excluded solely because they do not explicitly declare `use: sig`.

expectation.grounded: `PyJWKClient.get_signing_keys()` should include `PyJWK` entries whose `public_key_use` is either `"sig"` or absent (`None`), provided the key has a `key_id`. If no such keys are present, it should continue to raise `PyJWKClientError`.
expectation.conceptual: Signing-key lookup should treat a missing JWK use declaration as compatible with signing, while still returning only keys that are identifiable and still failing clearly when the JWKS does not contain any usable signing keys.

constraints.grounded: Do not broaden signing-key selection beyond JWKs whose use is explicitly signing or unspecified. Keys must still have a `key_id` to be returned, and the existing failure mode for an empty eligible result set must remain a `PyJWKClientError`.
constraints.conceptual: The update should expand compatibility for valid JWKS documents without weakening key filtering rules or changing the way missing usable signing keys are reported.

behavior: `PyJWKClient.get_signing_keys()` now considers JWKs with an omitted `use` value as signing-capable candidates.
A JWK is returned as a signing key only if it both qualifies by use (`sig` or unspecified) and has a key ID.
JWKs whose use is not signing and not omitted continue to be excluded from signing-key results.
When no eligible signing keys are found after applying the filter, `PyJWKClientError` is still raised.
acceptance_criteria: When a JWKS contains a key with `kid` present and `use` set to `sig`, `PyJWKClient.get_signing_keys()` should return that key as before.
When a JWKS contains a key with `kid` present and no `use` claim, `PyJWKClient.get_signing_keys()` should return that key as an eligible signing key.
When a JWKS contains keys without a `kid`, those keys should not be returned as signing keys even if their `use` is `sig` or omitted.
When a JWKS contains no keys that satisfy the signing-key eligibility rules, `PyJWKClient.get_signing_keys()` should raise `PyJWKClientError`.

task_1.title: Reject unsupported keyword arguments in decode APIs
task_1.description: Version 2.2.0 tightens the JWT/JWS decode API surface so that only documented decode parameters are accepted. Unsupported keyword arguments are no longer silently ignored, while claim validation inputs such as audience, issuer, and leeway remain supported through explicit parameters.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that JWT and JWS decoding only accept the documented decode parameters and fail fast when callers pass unsupported keyword arguments, instead of silently ignoring those inputs.

expectation.grounded: The public decode entry points should expose explicit support for `audience`, `issuer`, and `leeway` on `PyJWT.decode_complete` and `PyJWT.decode`, and should no longer accept arbitrary extra keyword arguments on `PyJWT` or `PyJWS` decode methods. Decode calls that include unsupported keywords should fail at call time rather than being ignored. Claim validation should continue to use the supplied `audience`, `issuer`, and `leeway` values when validating decoded payloads.
expectation.conceptual: Decoding should match the documented API exactly: supported validation options remain available, and any unknown decode option should be treated as an error instead of being silently accepted.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the observable decode contract for supported parameters such as `audience`, `issuer`, `leeway`, `key`, `algorithms`, and `options`. Successful decode flows should still return decoded payload data, and claim validation should still run against the provided validation inputs.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should be strict about invalid inputs without regressing normal decoding behavior for valid, supported arguments.

behavior: `PyJWT.decode_complete` accepts explicit `audience`, `issuer`, and `leeway` parameters for claim validation instead of a generic extra-keyword bucket.
`PyJWT.decode` accepts the same explicit validation parameters and forwards them into payload claim validation.
`PyJWS.decode_complete` and `PyJWS.decode` no longer accept arbitrary extra keyword arguments.
Passing an unsupported keyword argument to the decode APIs now results in an argument error instead of the library silently ignoring the value.
When `audience`, `issuer`, or `leeway` are provided through the supported API, decode behavior continues to validate claims against those values.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller decodes a token with supported parameters such as `audience`, `issuer`, or `leeway`, the decode operation should continue to perform claim validation using those values.
When a caller passes an unknown keyword argument to a JWT decode API, the call should fail immediately instead of proceeding with the unknown option ignored.
When a caller passes an unknown keyword argument to a JWS decode API, the call should fail immediately instead of proceeding with the unknown option ignored.
When a caller uses only the documented decode parameters, successful decode calls should still return the decoded payload as before.

task_2.title: Adopt timezone-aware UTC handling for JWT claim validation
task_2.description: The 2.2.0 upgrade modernizes JWT time handling by evaluating time-based claims against timezone-aware UTC instead of naive UTC, and it makes the decode API explicitly expose audience, issuer, and leeway as supported parameters. This preserves JWT validation behavior while aligning the library with current Python datetime guidance.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 2.2.0 preserves JWT decoding behavior while using timezone-aware UTC semantics for time-based claims and relying on the library's explicit decode parameters for audience, issuer, and leeway.

expectation.grounded: In 2.2.0, `PyJWT.decode` accepts `audience`, `issuer`, and `leeway` as explicit public parameters and still returns the decoded payload. Claim validation derives the current comparison timestamp from a timezone-aware UTC datetime before evaluating `exp`, `iat`, and `nbf`. `leeway` remains supported as either a numeric seconds value or a `timedelta`, and audience input is constrained to a string, an iterable of audience values, or `None`.
expectation.conceptual: JWT decoding should continue to work with the documented claim-validation inputs, but time-based claims must now be interpreted against the current UTC time using timezone-aware semantics. Consumers should call the decode API through its supported audience, issuer, and leeway arguments rather than depending on unspecified extra keyword forwarding.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the successful decode result shape: `PyJWT.decode` should still return the payload mapping. Preserve support for `leeway` as seconds or `timedelta`, preserve audience handling for string, iterable, or `None`, and do not rely on arbitrary extra keyword arguments being accepted by `PyJWT.decode`.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing JWT validation outcomes stable for supported inputs while modernizing UTC time handling. The upgrade should narrow integrations to the documented decode contract without introducing unrelated behavior changes.

behavior: `jwt.decode`/`PyJWT.decode` exposes `audience`, `issuer`, and `leeway` as explicit supported parameters instead of generic keyword passthrough.
Validation of `exp`, `iat`, and `nbf` uses the current UTC time derived from a timezone-aware datetime.
When `leeway` is provided as a `timedelta`, it is interpreted as an equivalent number of seconds during claim evaluation.
Unsupported extra keyword arguments are no longer part of the accepted public decode call surface.
acceptance_criteria: When an application decodes a JWT with `jwt.decode`, it should be able to supply `audience`, `issuer`, and `leeway` through the method's documented parameters and receive the decoded payload on success.
When a JWT includes `exp`, `iat`, or `nbf`, the library should evaluate those claims against the current UTC time using timezone-aware semantics.
When `leeway` is passed as a `timedelta`, the decode operation should honor it the same way as an equivalent seconds value during time-based claim checks.
When callers pass unspecified extra keyword arguments to `jwt.decode`, the upgrade should treat those arguments as unsupported rather than silently forwarding them.

task_4.title: Honor JWT header algorithm during encoding
task_4.description: The 2.2.0 update changes JWT encoding so that a caller-provided header algorithm is honored as the effective signing algorithm. This lets applications supply the desired algorithm through the JWT headers and ensures that, when both a header algorithm and the encode argument are present, the header value takes precedence instead of being ignored.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `jwt.encode()` honors a caller-provided JWT header algorithm so applications can control the encoded token's algorithm through the header, including when the `algorithm` argument is omitted or conflicts with the header value.

expectation.grounded: When `jwt.encode()` is called with a non-empty `headers["alg"]`, encoding should use that header value as the effective algorithm for the token header and signing flow instead of the `algorithm` parameter. If both `headers["alg"]` and `algorithm` are provided and differ, `headers["alg"]` should win without requiring a conflict error. If `headers["alg"]` is absent or empty, existing `algorithm` handling should continue, including the default of `"none"` when no algorithm argument is supplied.
expectation.conceptual: Encoding a JWT should respect the algorithm declared in the supplied headers. A header-specified algorithm should override any separate algorithm argument, while existing behavior should remain unchanged when no usable header algorithm is provided.

constraints.grounded: The change is limited to encode-time algorithm selection in `jwt.encode()` / JWS encoding. It should not alter behavior for calls that do not supply a truthy `headers["alg"]`, and it should preserve the prior fallback behavior when no explicit algorithm source is available.
constraints.conceptual: Only requests that explicitly provide a usable header algorithm should behave differently. All other encoding scenarios should continue to work as before.

behavior: A non-empty `headers["alg"]` becomes the effective algorithm used during JWT encoding.
If `headers["alg"]` and the `algorithm` argument disagree, the header value takes precedence.
Supplying `headers["alg"]` allows callers to drive algorithm selection even when the `algorithm` argument is omitted.
If `headers["alg"]` is missing or empty, encoding continues to rely on the `algorithm` argument and its existing default behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller encodes a token with `headers` containing a non-empty `alg`, the resulting token should be encoded using that algorithm.
When a caller provides both `headers["alg"]` and an `algorithm` argument with different values, encoding should follow the header algorithm rather than the argument value.
When a caller omits the `algorithm` argument but provides a non-empty `headers["alg"]`, encoding should still use the header algorithm.
When a caller does not provide a usable `headers["alg"]`, encode behavior should remain consistent with prior releases.

task_5.title: Treat null JWT audience claims as absent during decode validation
task_5.description: PyJWT 2.2.0 fixes audience validation so tokens whose `aud` claim is null are handled like tokens without an audience claim. Decoding no longer incorrectly requires an `audience` argument for that case, while explicit audience checks still fail when the token does not provide a usable audience value.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that JWT decoding treats a token audience claim of `null` as absent for audience validation, so tokens with `{"aud": null}` can be decoded without supplying `audience`, while still failing appropriately when an audience is explicitly required or when a real audience claim does not match.

expectation.grounded: During `decode()` audience validation, treat a missing or empty `aud` claim value the same way when deciding whether audience verification can proceed. If `audience` is not provided and the token has no usable `aud` claim, decoding should continue without raising `InvalidAudienceError`. If `audience` is provided but the token has no usable `aud` claim, raise `MissingRequiredClaimError` for `aud`. Existing `InvalidAudienceError` behavior should remain for tokens that do carry a non-empty `aud` claim when no `audience` is supplied or when none of the supplied audience values match.
expectation.conceptual: Decoding should no longer treat `aud: null` as a real audience that forces callers to pass an audience. A null or otherwise unusable audience claim should behave like an absent claim: harmless when no audience check is requested, but rejected as missing when the caller explicitly asks to validate an audience.

constraints.grounded: Do not relax validation for tokens with a real `aud` claim. `decode()` must still reject tokens that contain a non-empty audience when the caller omits `audience`, and it must still raise `InvalidAudienceError` when provided audience values do not match the token's `aud` claim. Preserve support for string and collection audience claims during matching.
constraints.conceptual: Only the null or effectively absent audience case should change. Normal audience-enforcement behavior for present audience values must remain intact, including rejection of unexpected or mismatched audiences.

behavior: If `decode()` is called without an `audience` argument and the token has no `aud` claim, audience validation is skipped.
If `decode()` is called without an `audience` argument and the token's `aud` claim is null or otherwise empty, audience validation is skipped instead of raising `InvalidAudienceError`.
If `decode()` is called with an `audience` argument and the token has no `aud` claim, or its `aud` claim is null or otherwise empty, decoding raises `MissingRequiredClaimError` for `aud`.
If `decode()` is called without an `audience` argument and the token has a non-empty `aud` claim, decoding raises `InvalidAudienceError`.

If `decode()` is called with an `audience` argument and the token has a non-empty `aud` claim, decoding succeeds only when at least one supplied audience value matches; otherwise it raises `InvalidAudienceError`.
acceptance_criteria: When a JWT is decoded without providing `audience` and its payload contains `aud: null`, it should decode successfully without an audience-validation error.
When a JWT is decoded with an explicit `audience` and its payload contains `aud: null`, it should fail with `MissingRequiredClaimError` for `aud`.
When a JWT is decoded without providing `audience` and it contains a non-empty `aud` claim, it should still fail with `InvalidAudienceError`.
When a JWT is decoded with an explicit `audience` and it contains a non-empty `aud` claim that does not include any requested audience, it should still fail with `InvalidAudienceError`.
When a JWT is decoded with an explicit `audience` and it contains a matching non-empty `aud` claim, it should continue to decode successfully.

task_7.title: Remove the cryptography upper-version cap
task_7.description: Version 2.2.0 broadens dependency compatibility by removing the upper bound on the optional `cryptography` package. This lets consumers install or resolve the library alongside newer major `cryptography` releases without being blocked by an artificial version cap, while preserving existing runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 2.2.0 no longer blocks users from installing or resolving the library with newer major versions of `cryptography` solely because of an upper dependency bound.

expectation.grounded: The library's published dependency constraints should no longer impose an upper version limit on `cryptography`. Environments that use `cryptography` for supported features should be able to install and resolve the package with newer major `cryptography` releases, and no public JWT APIs or cryptography-backed feature contracts should change as part of this update.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to adopt newer `cryptography` releases without the library refusing installation due to outdated version pinning. The upgrade is compatibility-focused and should not otherwise change how the library behaves.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce new public API requirements, new runtime errors, or changed success/failure semantics for existing JWT operations as part of removing the `cryptography` upper bound. The change should broaden dependency resolution only, not alter the observable behavior of supported cryptography-backed functionality.
constraints.conceptual: The update should only relax dependency compatibility. Existing application behavior should remain the same apart from no longer being blocked from using newer compatible `cryptography` versions.

behavior: The package no longer declares an upper version cap for `cryptography`.
Dependency resolution should permit installation with newer major `cryptography` releases that were previously excluded by version metadata alone.
The upgrade does not add new user-facing runtime features or change existing JWT API behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer installs or resolves version 2.2.0 in an environment with a newer major `cryptography` release, the dependency metadata should not reject that environment solely because of an upper bound.
When applications continue using existing JWT functionality after upgrading to 2.2.0, they should observe the same public API behavior as before.
When `cryptography` is present at a newer major version, the upgrade should be treated as a compatibility allowance rather than a runtime feature change.

task_6.title: Allow encoding JWTs without a typ header
task_6.description: The 2.2.0 update changes JWT/JWS encoding so the header type field is no longer mandatory. Callers can still override the token type with a custom value, and they can now intentionally omit the `typ` header to align with RFC7519 behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that applications can generate JWT/JWS tokens without a `typ` header when needed for standards compliance, while preserving support for explicit custom `typ` header values during encoding.

expectation.grounded: When encoding tokens through the library's JWT/JWS encode APIs, the `headers` argument must continue to allow overriding the header `typ` value with a non-empty custom value. If `headers` provides `typ` as a falsey value, the encoded token header must omit `typ` instead of emitting the library's default `typ` entry.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to create tokens with either a custom type header or no type header at all. The library should no longer force a `typ` header onto encoded tokens when the caller explicitly clears it.

constraints.grounded: This change must be backward compatible for existing encode calls that rely on the default header or pass a non-empty `typ`. Other header entries supplied through `headers` must still be preserved, and only the presence of `typ` should change when the caller explicitly clears it.
constraints.conceptual: Existing token generation behavior should remain unchanged unless the caller intentionally suppresses the type header. The update should narrow the change to header output semantics rather than altering unrelated encoding behavior.

behavior: Encoded JWT/JWS headers continue to accept a caller-specified non-empty `typ` value and serialize it as the header type.
If the caller supplies `typ` as a falsey value in the encode headers, the resulting token header excludes `typ` entirely.
Header merging still applies normally, so custom headers remain included alongside the updated `typ` handling.
acceptance_criteria: When a token is encoded without overriding `typ`, it should retain the library's existing default behavior.
When a token is encoded with a non-empty custom `typ` header value, the resulting token should expose that custom `typ` value.
When a token is encoded with `typ` explicitly cleared through the headers input, the resulting token should not contain a `typ` header field.
When additional custom headers are provided together with the `typ` setting, the other custom headers should still appear in the encoded token header.

task_8.title: Expand EdDSA support to Ed448 and OKP keys
task_8.description: Version 2.2.0 broadens EdDSA support from Ed25519-only handling to Octet Key Pair support that also includes Ed448, updates JWK import and export behavior for both curves, and exposes the generalized algorithm through the renamed OKPAlgorithm class.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that EdDSA supports both Ed25519 and Ed448 Octet Key Pair keys, and that integrations using the previous Ed25519-specific algorithm class are aligned with the generalized OKP algorithm interface.

expectation.grounded: The default algorithm registry should resolve "EdDSA" to `OKPAlgorithm`. Public integrations that directly referenced `Ed25519Algorithm` should use `OKPAlgorithm`, whose `prepare_key`, `verify`, `to_jwk`, and `from_jwk` behavior now covers both Ed25519 and Ed448 key pairs. `from_jwk` should accept only OKP JWKs whose `crv` is `Ed25519` or `Ed448`, return the corresponding public or private key type, and raise `InvalidKeyError` for unsupported curves or malformed key parameters.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to sign, verify, import, and export EdDSA keys for both Ed25519 and Ed448 through the generalized OKP algorithm interface, while invalid or unsupported OKP key material is still rejected in a consistent way.

constraints.grounded: Existing Ed25519 EdDSA behavior must remain compatible after the upgrade. Verification must continue to return a success or failure result without changing the API shape, including when a private OKP key object is supplied for verification. JWK handling must remain limited to OKP keys and reject unsupported curve values or invalid key bytes with `InvalidKeyError`.
constraints.conceptual: Do not regress existing Ed25519 EdDSA flows while adding Ed448 support. Keep the verification contract stable, preserve JWK round-tripping for supported OKP keys, and continue rejecting malformed or unsupported keys instead of silently accepting them.

behavior: The default `EdDSA` algorithm is backed by `OKPAlgorithm` rather than an Ed25519-only implementation.
The public EdDSA algorithm class is generalized from `Ed25519Algorithm` to `OKPAlgorithm`.
`OKPAlgorithm.prepare_key` accepts Ed25519 and Ed448 private or public key objects, as well as serialized key input that resolves to those key types.
`OKPAlgorithm.verify` supports Ed25519 and Ed448 keys and may be given either a public key or a private key object for verification.
`OKPAlgorithm.to_jwk` exports OKP JWKs that identify the correct curve for either Ed25519 or Ed448 keys.
`OKPAlgorithm.from_jwk` parses OKP JWKs for both Ed25519 and Ed448 and rejects unsupported curves or malformed parameters with `InvalidKeyError`.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller signs with `EdDSA` using an Ed25519 key pair, signing and verification should continue to work as before.
When a caller signs with `EdDSA` using an Ed448 key pair, the resulting signature should verify successfully with the matching Ed448 public key.
When an integration uses `OKPAlgorithm` directly, it should be able to prepare, verify, serialize, and parse both Ed25519 and Ed448 OKP keys through the same public interface.
When `to_jwk` is used on a supported OKP key, the exported JWK should preserve the correct curve identity and be usable by `from_jwk` for the same key type.
When `from_jwk` receives an OKP JWK with an unsupported curve value or malformed key material, it should reject the input with `InvalidKeyError`.

When verification is performed with a private Ed25519 or Ed448 key object instead of its public key, a valid signature should still verify successfully and an invalid signature should fail verification.
